active_goal.objective: Ship a production-ready, self-contained Rust BORSUK ANN library on S3/blob storage that beats BOTH S3 Vectors and Turbopuffer at equal or better recall on matched end-to-end p90/p95 latency and throughput per total dollar. This is a product goal, not a report. Support incremental insert/update/delete, authenticated generation-pinned publication and reads, bounded RAM/cache/concurrency, restart/recovery, and in-process automatic or callable compaction/GC; require no separate maintenance instance. Preserve current V282 on-demand SQ8 work and live jobs; do not duplicate consultations or paid runs. Opus 5.5 estimates the current PQ64 plus f32 summary/unit router at 184 resident bytes per row, or about 18.4 GB at 100M D768, before old-generation pinning. This is a projection, not a measurement. Reconcile prior V139/V146/V149/V150 centroid-page failures and the completed Fable review before choosing any new arm; do not repeat a known failure. Predeclare a feasible 100M RAM, GET, byte, p90 and cost envelope. Prefer a small resident router and one parallel S3 fetch wave, but choose memory versus quality from a measured Pareto curve, not an arbitrary 2 GB cap. Candidate design: balanced hierarchical semantic cells with physical locality and boundary coverage; scan small SQ8 leaves, split skewed/diffuse leaves, use local compressed indexing only where measured cell-specific gains justify it. Avoid S3 graph pointer chasing and full-vector/full-graph hydration. First run the cheapest distinct paired 100k D768 cosine k100 falsifier on ReLAION and CoHere against unchanged V282, decomposing exact-GT loss into router, selected-cell coverage, local index and SQ8 quantization and counting GETs, bytes, RAM and route CPU. Use V282 98% mean recall@100, p05 95, 32 GET and 16 MiB caps unless a redesign is predeclared; kill weak arms early. Freeze a winner for fresh 1M cold HTTP, then 10M and 100M scale. Measure p50/p90/p95/p99, QPS, RSS including generation swap, physical S3 requests/bytes/retries/errors, build and incremental-maintenance cost, total lifecycle cost and failure recovery. Compare competitors on identical corpus, query split, metric, k, filters, cache state, region and concurrency; if only published targets are available, cite date/configuration and label mismatches, never claim a measured win. When a gate fails, redesign routing, layout, quantization or fetch schedule with one causal change per experiment. Unreleased formats need no backward compatibility. Push code, tests, receipts and a concise decision table to BORSUK main. Within 24 hours deliver one substantive object-native library increment and a falsifiable next gate, then continue until the product works.

What this change does: The draft uses the payload’s saved cgroup path and avoids stopping an already absent cgroup when both exit receipts are zero. That addresses the recorded failure, but two gaps remain before runtime qualification.

**Must fix:**

1. **Cgroup disappearance can still produce a false INVALID96.** At [line 24](/tmp/borsuk-scale-parity-qualification-a0003/user-data.lifecycle-repair.pending.sh:24), the directory can disappear after the existence check but before `systemctl stop`, reproducing “Unit not loaded.” At [line 29](/tmp/borsuk-scale-parity-qualification-a0003/user-data.lifecycle-repair.pending.sh:29), disappearance between checking and reading `cgroup.events` also produces 96.

   Minimal fix: reconcile these failures against the exact saved path afterward. Accept a confirmed unloading/disappearance case only with both zero exit receipts. Keep manager timeouts, other errors, and earlier failures sticky; never reset the accumulated status to zero. Otherwise, successful runs can still fail solely because collection raced with cleanup.

2. **The later absent-cgroup branch bypasses the exit-receipt requirement.** [Line 31](/tmp/borsuk-scale-parity-qualification-a0003/user-data.lifecycle-repair.pending.sh:31) accepts disappearance after stopping without checking `launcher.exit` and `final-exit`. With bootstrap status zero, successful stop, and a missing payload receipt, that branch can report success. The frozen payload normally writes its receipt before successful exit, but the collector does not enforce the requested invariant.

   Minimal fix: apply the same two-zero-receipt requirement to every accepted absence. For missing or malformed saved paths, record “path unverified” rather than `owned-cgroup-absent`; retain INVALID96 and avoid using the unvalidated path for cleanup.

The remaining design is sound: exact path matching rejects unexpected paths, bounded stop preserves the safety limit, and `populated 0` covers live processes throughout the cgroup’s descendants. An empty top-level `cgroup.procs` would provide weaker evidence. [Linux cgroup documentation](https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html#un-populated-notification)

Keep this repair around saved identity and final drain state. Retaining the unit with `--remain-after-exit` would require changing the existing `--wait --pipe` launch arrangement; systemd documents those options as incompatible. [systemd-run documentation](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/man/systemd-run.xml)

Proposed small EC2 smokes, using tiny shell payloads and fresh output prefixes:

| Case | Required observation |
|---|---|
| Clean exit 0; unit already unloaded | Exact saved path, both receipts zero, cgroup absent; closure 0. |
| Payload exits 17 | Nonzero original/launcher/payload evidence preserved; never success. |
| Missing, empty, multiline, or wrong saved path | INVALID96; no stop based on that value; no authenticated-absence claim. |
| Missing/nonzero exit receipt when cgroup disappears after stop | INVALID96. |
| Cgroup disappears between check/stop or check/read | Confirmed disappearance plus zero receipts succeeds; unrelated errors remain INVALID. |
| Live child at collector entry | Record `populated 1` and child membership first; bounded stop must establish absence or `populated 0`. Remaining population or timeout stays INVALID. |

The remaining-process smoke must prove the child is alive **at collector entry**. Merely backgrounding a child can test systemd’s automatic cleanup before the collector runs. `KillMode=control-group` already terminates remaining processes on stop. [systemd kill documentation](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/man/systemd.kill.xml)

Its recorded six successful compiler stages, 86-test result, and 436 before/after source checks belong to source `afb70da…`, independently of wrapper qualification. Preserve the archive and cleanup receipts; make no retroactive GO or performance claim. Wrapper smokes do not require another compiler run.
